system.scope: U.S. carriage of defined letters over post routes

date.label: Private Express Statutes as presently in force (U.S.C. / CFR)

control_mechanism.statement: Statutory restriction on compensated private carriage of letters over post routes, with legislatively and regulatorily defined exceptions and suspensions.

evidence_bindings.claim: Federal law restricts private express carriage of letters over post routes
evidence_bindings.source: 18 U.S.C. § 1696 — Private express for letters and packets
evidence_bindings.fact: Federal law establishes penalties for establishing a private express for the conveyance of letters or packets over post routes, subject to enumerated statutory exceptions.

evidence_bindings.claim: Exclusivity is bounded and conditional for letters carried out of the mail
evidence_bindings.source: 39 U.S.C. § 601 — Letters carried out of the mail
evidence_bindings.fact: Defines the conditions under which a letter may lawfully be carried out of the mail (including specified price/weight and other regulatory conditions and exceptions).

evidence_bindings.claim: An implementing regulatory regime defines exceptions and suspensions
evidence_bindings.source: 39 CFR Part 310 — Enforcement of the Private Express Statutes
evidence_bindings.fact: A dedicated federal regulatory part exists specifically to enforce and define the operation of the Private Express Statutes, including exceptions and suspensions.

claim_boundary.admissible: Within the U.S. letter-carriage system, federal law creates a legal-exclusivity layer by restricting private carriage of defined letters over post routes, subject to enumerated exceptions and suspensions.
excluded: USPS has a legal monopoly over all mail.
Any claim extending the layer to parcels, freight, or electronic communication.
